note: Guard registry for gate.py. The module fails closed without this file, and refuses to load if any of the eight ids below is absent. Each guard is a rule about what a run is permitted to conclude, not about whether its arithmetic is correct.

guards.name: pre-registration
guards.rule: A run declares its question, statistic, and expected outcome before it executes, and closes against that declaration.
guards.fail_message: the run was not declared before it executed. what a run may conclude is fixed before it produces numbers, not after.
guards.rationale: Without a prior expectation there is no such thing as a surprising result, and any output can be narrated as confirmation. The declaration is what makes close() a comparison rather than a summary.

guards.name: statistic fits the question
guards.rule: The declared statistic must be shown to discriminate between the hypotheses actually in play.
guards.fail_message: the statistic is not shown to discriminate between the hypotheses in play.
guards.rationale: A statistic can be computed correctly, be reported honestly, and still be unable to tell the two candidate answers apart. That failure is invisible in the output and has to be caught at declaration time.

guards.name: resolution
guards.rule: The instrument scale, times a safety margin, must be finer than the feature the run must resolve.
guards.fail_message: the instrument is coarser than the feature it must resolve. a null from an instrument that could not have seen the feature is not evidence of absence.
guards.rationale: The most common way to find nothing is to look with something too coarse to have found it. Declaring both scales converts an unfalsifiable null into an arithmetic check that can be made before the run.

guards.name: controls
guards.rule: Every control is named with a predicted value before the run, and its observed value is recorded before close.
guards.fail_message: a control was not declared, carries no predicted value, or was declared and never run. an untested gate is not a passing gate.
guards.rationale: A detector that has never been shown to fire on a known positive cannot support a negative result. Recording predicted separately from observed also makes a failed control impossible to drop silently from the writeup.
guards.enforcement: deny at declaration, finding at close

guards.name: layer tagging
guards.rule: Every quantity is tagged generator, physical, or instrument, and names the object it is a property of. Crossing layers requires an explicit justification.
guards.fail_message: a quantity is untagged or crosses layers without justification. a property of the generator is not a property of the physical system.
guards.rationale: The characteristic self-confirmation failure is reading a structure back out of a model that was built to contain it. Tagging at record time makes the promotion an explicit, reviewable act rather than a silent one.

guards.name: dimensional integrity
guards.rule: A ratio is admissible only when numerator and denominator are properties of the same object.
guards.fail_message: a ratio was formed across two different objects. the quotient of a property of A by a property of B denotes nothing.
guards.rationale: Two quantities can be individually meaningful, share units, divide without error, and produce a number that refers to nothing. Comparing one statistic across two objects is fine; dividing a property of one by a property of the other is not.
guards.enforcement: void the ratio, record a finding

guards.name: named support
guards.rule: A claim names the recorded quantities that support it, and those quantities must exist.
guards.fail_message: a claim names no recorded quantity that supports it.
guards.rationale: Claims that name their support can be checked against the layer tags of what they rest on. Claims that do not are prose, and prose accumulates in a conclusion without ever passing a check.

guards.name: independence
guards.rule: Convergence across several lines may be asserted only after naming what those lines share.
guards.fail_message: convergence asserted without naming what the converging lines share. lines that share an input do not independently confirm.
guards.rationale: Agreement between analyses run on the same generated data measures the data, not the world. Naming the shared input does not forbid the claim; it downgrades it from independent confirmation to a qualified one.
guards.enforcement: record as qualified, or finding if nothing named
